thread:
alex: Paging — p99 inference latency jump on hosted cluster + increased 504s. Alerts started ~3123456700. Logs show long tail in token generation and a few retry storms. incident-bot created INC-2026-431. @jamie can you take initial triage?
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-431 created · Severity: P2 · Pager routed to eng-oncall · Channels: #eng-oncall #incidents · Runbook: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/inference-latency
jamie: I’m on it. quick glance at telemetry — CPU on gpu-host-12 spiked, queue depth up, we’re hitting max_in_flight=800 on hosted pool. Also seeing bursts from a client looped retries (x3).
alex: noted. first live mitigations: 1) reduce max_in_flight to limit queue depth; 2) apply per-route emergency rate-cap for /v1/generate; 3) temporarily disable streaming for the hosted tier (reduces scheduling overhead).
jamie: I'll apply (1) and (2) now. Bumping to low-risk changes.
jamie: Command I’m running:
```
# runtime CLI
redwoodctl runtime update --pool hosted --set max_in_flight=350
redwoodctl routing update-rate --route /v1/generate --burst 20 --rate 60
```
jamie: Applied. Watching metrics. queue depth dropped ~40% within 30s. p99 latency down a bit but errors still present (~2.5% 504).
sam-cs: Heads up — CS is getting tickets from AcmeCorp and Flowlytics about timeouts. AcmeCorp is on dedicated? They said hosted endpoints for some jobs. Sharing timestamps.
alex: @sam-cs thanks. We should consider temporarily exempting enterprise customers from global shedding and bump their per-minute quotas so they don't hit 429s while we stabilize. Lia, will you take that action if we decide?
lia: I can. If we bump too much we risk overload. Suggest targeted lifts: accounts [acme: +50r/min, flowlytics: +30r/min] and keep global route at conservative 60rps.
ajamie: Also toggling streaming off for hosted to reduce small-chunk context switching. Doing now.
jamie: Command: `redwoodctl feature toggle --pool hosted --feature streaming=false`
jamie: streaming disabled. Observability: per-token scheduling overhead dropped, error rate now ~1.2%. latency p99 trending down.
alex: Good. Next, we have to decide about shedding policy — current runtime policy prefers dropping long-running requests when queue > 600. I propose lowering threshold to 450 and reducing per-request timeout from 90s to 45s to fail fast and surface problems to clients rather than pile up. Thoughts?
lia: Agree for short term. Fail-fast makes retries visible rather than cascades. We should communicate in incident notes that we reduced timeouts.
jamie: Implementing shedding threshold change: `redwoodctl runtime set-shedding --pool hosted --queue-threshold 450 --max-runtime 45s`
jamie: Done. Immediately seeing fewer queued requests; throughput holds. 504s falling to ~0.6%.
sam-cs: We just informed AcmeCorp support rep and offered to whitelist some jobs for a short window. They accepted the temporary quota bump.
alex: Logging actions in the incident timeline. Assigning tasks: jamie — keep mitigation for next 30m and monitor graphs; lia — perform targeted quota changes and own customer comms; sam-cs — collate customer impact list and affected endpoints; alex — escalate to eng-runtime if metrics don't normalize within 45m.
jamie: Ack. Adding dashboards and key traces to the incident ticket.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-431 update · Status: Mitigated (partial) · Actions: max_in_flight lowered, streaming disabled, rate-limit applied, shedding threshold adjusted · Next: continue observation · Pager: next oncall @lia at 23:00 UTC
lia: I’ll take the handoff at 23:00 UTC. Please include the runbook snippet and links to the kibana query I used: `kql: service:inference AND response:504 AND timestamp >= now()-1h`
alex: Thanks team. If things remain stable for 45m we can move to monitor-only and start postmortem prep. If errors resurge, escalate to runtime infra for kernel/packing investigation.
lia: acked. leaving notes for night oncall: avoid increasing max_in_flight; prefer tightening shedding or routing to dedicated pools if traffic keeps rising.
jamie: leaving logs and commands in the incident ticket. handing off to @lia.
lia: Taking it. I'll push follow-up RFC for more graceful per-customer backoff later.
alex: Postmortem owners: jamie (mitigations timeline), lia (customer impact + quota playbook), runtime team requested to investigate root cause. Closing live thread and switching to incident tracker for details. :white_check_mark:
